extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, peer-review researchers, and journal reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical pilot and recommendations for implementing structured peer review questions in journal manuscript evaluation, including the specific questions to ask reviewers, recommended answer formats, coding/analysis approaches, and operational guidance for journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1: Clarity of objectives and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the objectives and the rationale of the study clearly stated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should indicate whether study objectives and rationale are clearly presented; in the recommended set this is phrased as 'Are the primary (and secondary) objectives clearly stated at the end of the introduction?'. Authors/editors can use this as an explicit checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2 (pilot): Methods reported for replicability/reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, is the application/theory/method/study reported in sufficient detail to allow for its replicability and/or reproducibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether methods are described with enough detail for replication; longest answers in pilot were for this question. Consider asking as multiple-choice with an option to provide concrete suggestions for missing detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3 (pilot): Appropriateness and description of statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, are statistical analyses, controls, sampling mechanism, and statistical reporting (e.g., P-values, CIs, effect sizes) appropriate and well described?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate both appropriateness and the adequacy of reporting (e.g., effect sizes, CIs). This was among the lowest agreement items, so consider prompting for specifics or requesting additional analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4 (pilot): Tables and figures — need for change
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the manuscript benefit from additional tables or figures, or from improving or removing (some of the) existing ones?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This question in the pilot used opposite answer directionality to some items (yes = needs change). The authors recommend rephrasing for consistent answer direction across questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5 (pilot): Interpretation supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, are the interpretation of results and study conclusions supported by the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether conclusions are justified by analyses and study design. This item had relatively low inter-reviewer agreement; reviewers may have differing thresholds for acceptable interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q6 (pilot): Emphasis of study strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors clearly emphasized the strengths of their study/theory/methods/argument?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note whether the manuscript highlights its strengths; pilot showed this was infrequently requested in traditional reports, so including this explicitly can nudge reviewers to comment on strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q7 (pilot): Statement of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors clearly stated the limitations of their study/methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check whether limitations are explicitly listed and suggest missing or understated limitations. In pilot this question commonly had reviewers pointing to Comments-to-Author or attachments for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q8 (pilot): Manuscript structure, flow, and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript structure, flow or writing need improving (e.g., the addition of subheadings, shortening of text, reorganization of sections, or moving details from one section to another)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, organization, and structure. This item had the highest (partial) agreement in the pilot (72%), possibly because structure conventions are shared within disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q9 (pilot): Need for language editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the manuscript benefit from language editing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the pilot Q9 was a mandatory yes/no drop-down with no free-text; recommended to allow comments. Agreement was moderate (58%); thresholds for acceptable language vary between reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Introduction question: background/literature appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the background and literature section up to date and appropriate for the topic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess currency and relevance of literature cited, conceptual framing, and whether background supports the study rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Introduction question: objectives stated
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the primary (and secondary) objectives clearly stated at the end of the introduction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures objectives are explicit and located where readers expect them; helps standardize reviewer focus on study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Methods question: methods reported in sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the study methods (including theory/applicability/modelling) reported in sufficient detail to allow for their replicability or reproducibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to pilot Q2; emphasizes inclusion of necessary materials, parameters, algorithms, data/code availability where relevant. Recommend multiple-choice answer with space for constructive suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Methods question: statistical and sampling appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are statistical analyses, controls, sampling mechanism, and statistical reporting (e.g., P-values, CIs, effect sizes) appropriate and well described?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same substance as pilot Q3; prompt reviewers to indicate missing analyses or reporting shortcomings (e.g., absent effect sizes, CIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Results question: results presentation and tables/figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the results presentation, including the number of tables and figures, appropriate to best present the study findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether results are presented clearly and whether figures/tables aid understanding; suggest additions/removals or reorganization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Results question: need for additional analyses/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Are additional sub-analyses or statistical measures needed (e.g., reporting of CIs, effect sizes, sensitivity analyses)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to identify specific additional analyses that would strengthen inference or robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Discussion question: interpretation supported by design/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the interpretation of results and study conclusions supported by the data and the study design?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to pilot Q5; emphasizes matching conclusions to study design limitations and analyses. Low agreement on this topic suggests need for clear prompts and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Discussion question: limitations emphasized
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors clearly emphasized the limitations of their study/theory/methods/argument?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same focus as pilot Q7; ask reviewers to list missing limitations or suggest clearer presentation of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer options and recommended response format
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend multiple-choice style answers with the last option providing a free-text field for constructive suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended choices: [ ] Not Applicable; [ ] Beyond my expertise, additional reviewer(s) should be consulted; [ ] Yes; [ ] No, the authors should (consider): (please list and number in the text field below Your suggestions so that the author/s can more easily follow your instructions or provide rebuttals). Implement as MCQs with text input to facilitate rater agreement calculation and readability for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform answer directionality across questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions should be phrased so that the meaning of 'Yes' (or other chosen primary label) is consistent across all questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot found some questions (e.g., Q4, Q8, Q9) had opposite directionality (yes = needs change). Modify wording so answer direction and options are the same across all questions to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate answer fields (avoid redirects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should answer the structured questions in their designated fields, not simply point to Comments-to-Author or attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot coded whether reviewers answered in the correct fields or directed to Comments-to-Author/attachments. Journals should encourage in-field responses to improve clarity and automated processing; if attachments are necessary, provide clear prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Comments-to-Author and Comments-to-Editor fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide open-text fields for additional comments to authors and confidential comments to editors, available after structured questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fields can capture broader feedback beyond structured questions. Pilot found many reviewers copied full traditional reports into Comments-to-Author; servers should allow but advise reviewers about intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding scheme for answers (pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories applied when coding reviewer answers: 1) yes; 2) no; 3) not applicable; 4) yes, and provided comments to the authors on how to address the issue; 5) no, and provided comments to the authors on how to address the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing answers, code into these categories. For inter-rater agreement classification between two reviewers use: A) agreement (same category), B) disagreement (different categories), C) partial agreement (e.g., yes vs yes+comments), D) unable to assess (one skipped, N/A or pointed to attachment). Consider grouping A and C as '(partial) agreement' for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater agreement metrics and statistical comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure percentage agreement per question and absolute agreement for final recommendations; use chi-square tests to compare agreement across fields and IF quartiles and with pre-implementation baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot reported per-question (partial) agreement percentages and compared absolute agreement for final recommendations to Elsevier Peer Review Workbench baseline; include statistical tests (chi-square) and p-values when comparing groups. Use clear denominators (e.g., percent of manuscripts N=107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer-length and report-length metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number of words per answer/text field and for full Comments-to-Author reports using median (Md) and interquartile range (IQR); use means for comparisons where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot used median/IQR due to non-normal distribution, Kruskal–Wallis tests for between-group comparisons, and reported mean when comparing to external sources (e.g., Web of Science). Use consistent word-count formulas and report both median/IQR and mean ± SD if useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational recommendation: system implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: If submission systems allow, implement questions as multiple-choice (with last option requiring text input), allow attachments, and provide Comments-to-Author and Comments-to-Editor fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates automated agreement calculation and readability for authors. Ensure question bank is adaptable by editors to field-specific needs; Elsevier provides a question bank as an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational recommendation: reviewer and author communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Alert reviewers in advance about the structured questions and encourage answering them while reading/evaluating the manuscript; inform authors which questions will be used to judge manuscripts so they can self-evaluate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot suggests advance notice improves uptake and may reduce mismatches (e.g., 'Reviewer 2' problem). Encourage reviewers not to paste pre-prepared reports into structured fields but to address the structured items directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of structured questions as author self-review checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that authors be told which structured questions will be used, and encourage them to use the same questions to self-evaluate and improve manuscripts before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This increases transparency and may improve manuscript quality prior to review.
